fiches.contexte: Spleen Qi Deficiency with Dampness, Liver Qi Stagnation, discomfort in the throat (Mei He Qi, “plum-pit throat”), nausea and fatigue.

principe.fr: Free the Liver, strengthen the Spleen

fiches.consigne: Dry, without oil, for a better grip. One session a day, ideally in the morning. On paired points, the timer restarts for the other side.
fiches.note: For nausea, PC 6 on its own, at any time.

items.loc: Back of the hand, between the 1st and 2nd metacarpals, at the midpoint of the 2nd metacarpal on the thumb side.
items.act: With LR 3 (the Four Gates): moves Qi and Blood, frees the throat, calms the mind.

items.loc: Top of the foot, in the hollow between the 1st and 2nd metatarsals, in front of where their bases meet.
items.act: Relieves Liver Qi Stagnation, settles Liver Yang, calms the Shen (spirit).

items.loc: Center of the hollow above the breastbone, 0.5 cun above the top edge of the manubrium (the top of the breastbone).
items.act: Makes Qi descend, loosens the throat (Mei He Qi).

items.loc: Front of the forearm, 2 cun above the wrist crease, between the two tendons.
items.act: Makes Stomach Qi descend (nausea), opens the chest, calms the Shen (spirit).

items.loc: Midline, 4 cun above the navel, halfway between the navel and the base of the breastbone.
items.act: Front-Mu point of the Stomach: harmonizes the Middle Burner (digestion), transforms Dampness.

items.loc: Level with the navel, 2 cun on each side.
items.act: Front-Mu point of the Large Intestine: regulates the belly and bowel movements, drains Dampness.

items.loc: On the leg, halfway between the knee and the outer ankle bone, 2 finger-widths outside the crest of the shinbone.
items.act: Transforms Phlegm and Dampness, soothes the throat, calms the mind.

items.loc: Inner side of the leg, in the hollow below the medial condyle of the tibia (the inner bump below the knee).
items.act: Drains Dampness from the Lower Burner, soothes the knee.

items.loc: 3 cun below ST 35 (outer “eye” of the knee), 1 finger-width outside the crest of the shinbone.
items.act: Tonifies the Qi and Blood of the Spleen and Stomach, fights fatigue, strengthens the knee.

items.loc: 3 cun above the inner ankle bone, just behind the edge of the shinbone.
items.act: Nourishes Blood and Yin, tonifies the Spleen, calms the Shen (spirit) for better sleep.

fiches.contexte: Long-standing knee pain, relieved by warmth: Cold-Damp Bi (painful obstruction).

principe.fr: Warm the meridians, unblock the collaterals

fiches.consigne: During the day or after exercise, not right before bed. Clean, dry skin: no product before the moxa.
fiches.note: If the tip of your tongue turns red or your sleep gets worse, shorten the moxa on ST 36.

items.loc: Above the kneecap, in the hollow at the middle of its upper edge.
items.act: Moves Qi and Blood in the knee, eases pain and stiffness.

items.loc: Outer side of the leg, in the hollow in front of and below the head of the fibula.
items.act: Hui-Meeting point of the tendons: relaxes the tendons, soothes the knee, moves Liver Qi.

tech: Moxa 2–3 cm (about an inch) from the skin, slow circles above both hollows. Pull it away as soon as it stings.
items.loc: Knee bent, the two hollows on either side of the kneecap tendon: Du Bi on the outside, Nei Xi Yan on the inside.
items.act: Expels Cold-Damp from the knee, gets things moving, calms pain.

tech: Pecking moxa (bring it close, then away, again and again), until you feel a pleasant warmth and slight redness.
items.loc: 3 cun below ST 35, 1 finger-width outside the crest of the shinbone.
items.act: Warms and tonifies the Spleen and Stomach, transforms Dampness at its source, strengthens the knee.

tech: Circular rubbing around the kneecap, until absorbed.
items.loc: Wait 2 to 3 minutes after the moxa. All around the knee, focusing on the “eyes” of the knee and the hollow behind the knee.
items.act: Moves Qi and Blood, calms pain. On days without moxa, use red tiger balm instead.

produits.texte: First choice when warmth relieves the knee. Air out the room, keep a bowl for the ash, and put the stick out by smothering it.
At the end of the session, for massage. Moves Qi and Blood, calms pain.
On days without moxa, rubbed into the knee. Warming.
A neutral base for massaging longer, or for diluting an essential oil.
Only as an extra, always diluted: 2 to 3 drops in a teaspoon of oil. Never with moxa. Avoid if you take blood thinners or are allergic to aspirin.

fiches.regle: Never put heat on a product you have just applied: moxa first, product after.
